newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INTERVIEW - Ceramco underplayed model card.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Ceramco underplayed model card.

text.p: Ceramco Corp Ltd Executive Chairman David Appleby said the ceramics and lingerie maker had probably underplayed the asset it had in the form of its long term contract with Australian supermodel, Elle MacPherson.

Appleby told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday that the company had "dropped the ball a bit," in terms of improving its profile through its association with MacPherson, who regularly appears on the covers of international fashion magazines.
"If we were honest we have let ourselves down and have let down the Elle opportunity. That's an area we are addressing at present," Appleby said.
"Part of the discussions we are going to have is how we can maximise her profile better in terms of selling lingerie."
Discussions would centre around devoloping the Elle MacPherson range in Australasia.

"With all the big brands coming in, our feeling is that we could do more with the Elle brand, so we are just looking to give that more focus, take it up a little bit, and then have Bendon and Hickory come off that as supplementary brands."
Appleby said lingerie sales in October and November were encouraging, but still not strong. The market in Australia had been particularly flat, he said.

"It's looking okay but it's going to be the Christmas trade that's going to determine it. We are in the same situation as the retail-related sort of companies. It just depends a little on what happens over the next four or five weeks."
Ceramco suffered a NZ$1.6 million loss in the six months to September and its shares, which today traded at NZ$1.15, have been bouncing around historic lows for many months.
The company expects to break even in the current year and return to profitability in 1997/98.
Ceramco, under the stewardship of Charles Bidwell, began selling its many assets in the late 1980s, resuling in a large capital repayment for shareholders.
Appleby said the company today, with just two main areas of operation left, was therefore a completely different beast.

"Charles got it down to a stage where there really were only two businesses. So I suppose the question is whether you should go the full hog and sell the last two and give the shareholders back their money or run it pretty much as a dividend yield
Ceramco still enjoys signficant import protection, with a 30 percent import duty imposed on its foreign competitors.
New Zealand tariffs are due to be phased out progressively over the next four years, at which time offshore sourcing will become more of an issue for Ceramco, he said.
